gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a mainstream 15.6-inch laptop can have a USB-C port with no video at all: Lenovo's spec sheet for the IdeaPad 1 15IRU7 lists its USB-C as "support data transfer only" and caps the machine at "native display and 1 external monitor via HDMI", so a driver-free two-screen extender has one video output to work with.
standout_why: Compared against the two cited pages (itechguides 15-best, deskgearhq), theofficejournal's 15.6-inch page and our own dealectric.com/best-laptop-screen-extender. itechguides says only the generic "Charging-only USB-C cannot drive a native USB-C monitor" and "Look for DisplayPort Alt Mode". deskgearhq says "Every configuration connects over a single USB-C cable using DisplayPort Alt Mode" and never covers a laptop without it. theofficejournal says to check the laptop's documentation. Our page covers MST, DisplayLink and the base M1/M2/M3 one-display limit but has no sentence about 15.6-inch laptops or data-only USB-C on Windows machines. None names a 15.6-inch laptop whose maker states a data-only USB-C port and a one-external-display ceiling, or ties that to how many screens of a dual extender light up. The general Alt Mode warning is already in the rivals and in ChatGPT's own answer, so this is new and useful, not a clean 3.
decides: It splits the pick by the laptop's ports, which the shopper has not given. On a 15.6-inch laptop with data-only USB-C and one HDMI port (Lenovo's IdeaPad 1 15IRU7 is the sourced example), the safe pick is one added screen that takes HDMI for video and USB for power: the Mobile Pixels Duex Max DS has that path per our page's Mobile Pixels attribution. The driver-free FOPO S10 Dual 15.6-inch would have a single native video output to draw on there; this is my inference from Lenovo's display count and FOPO's "each screen needs its own video connection" wording for the S7, since FOPO's S10 page could not be opened today. Two added screens on such a laptop need a driver-based extender (FOPO S788 with UsbDisplay, or the Trio 3 Pro with Mobile Pixels' driver, both per our page), which sends video over USB data. On a 15.6-inch laptop with video-capable USB-C plus HDMI, or two video-capable USB-C ports, the FOPO S10 stays the size-matched two-screen pick. The Lenovo sheet also gives a real 15.6-inch body width, 360.2 mm, to check against a maker's fit range.
